shape.appetite: One host-owned source reader and one PostgreSQL proof. Keep current client evaluation and local mode. Extract a reusable adapter only if a second real driver proves the boundary useful.
shape.problem: The current analysis component uses client-side source rows. A database path must preserve field meaning, row identity, filter scope, inspection, and responsive interaction while fitting automated customer-specific hosting.
shape.recommended_shape: The customer host authenticates a read and resolves server-owned source definitions. A bounded reader uses a PostgreSQL transaction to load all approved fields and rows from one consistent snapshot, normalizes only declared supported values, and returns a complete-or-error bundle to the existing tables prop. The current evaluator and charts remain local. Start with a fixed host implementation and deterministic fake. Test a second driver only after PostgreSQL establishes a concrete shared boundary. Consider one narrow server row or aggregate request only if a named workload fails the snapshot budget and its semantic contract can be proven.
shape.simpler_counterproposal: Use only fixed host endpoint SQL with no reusable reader abstraction. Keep it if PostgreSQL is the only useful driver or the second proof does not reveal shared behavior.
success_moves: Use the existing tables prop and local evaluator so the first real-data path keeps stages, inspection, and chart behavior.
Keep source registration, authentication, credentials, SQL, and driver objects on the host; bind values and enforce independent limits.
Publish all sources atomically from one consistent snapshot, with explicit type, coverage, count, and identity metadata.
Use declared types and reject lossy values before data becomes editable; distinguish stable keys from snapshot-only occurrence identity.
Test semantics with a deterministic fake, then verify transaction, type, and cleanup behavior using disposable PostgreSQL fixtures.
Run a second driver only when it tests a shared boundary shown useful by the first proof; otherwise keep the fixed endpoint.

first_proof.question: Can one registered PostgreSQL source set be read as a complete, type-safe snapshot and preserve the existing local analysis experience?
first_proof.artifact: A deterministic fake and disposable PostgreSQL fixture produce the same bounded source bundle through ExplorEdaProject.tables.
first_proof.try: Load a small fixture with nulls, text, booleans, supported numbers/dates, a stable key and keyless duplicate rows. Run a filter and inspect source/result rows through the current evaluator. Inject a missing source, unsupported type, cap+1 rows, interruption, and a writer commit between source reads.
first_proof.observe: Values and types match the fixture oracle; nulls and identities remain distinct; all sources reflect one database snapshot; unsupported and interrupted reads publish nothing; bounds trigger before uncontrolled buffering; cleanup is observed; filter and inspection outputs match local arrays. Measure transfer and browser memory on a named fixture.
first_proof.decide: Proceed only when semantic and completion invariants hold and the agreed response/memory budget passes. Otherwise narrow supported data or compare one named remote demand. Add a second driver only if the PostgreSQL result identifies a useful common boundary.
first_proof.decision_rule: Any semantic loss, false completeness, mixed snapshot, uncertain cleanup, or missing workload budget fails the proof; transfer failure may trigger one narrow demand comparison.

rabbit_holes: A universal SQL or formula compiler before one server operation is admitted.
Cross-database federation and remote pagination before a named consumer needs them.
A second driver, package, or service without evidence that it reduces maintenance or unlocks a required runtime.
Performance claims based only on row count without width, types, memory, or filter timing.
